_document.title: MLLDE xAPI IRI Registry — unified identifiers for CEFR skills, subskills and measurement concepts
_document.changelog: v0.8 (2026-08-26, approved by AE): measurement-model / policy release — NO new IRIs (reuses v0.7.1 identifiers). MEDIATION: CA re-mapped to rubric/global-achievement (NOT interaction; +interaction only on facilitation descriptors facilitate-*/invite-*), and RAISED to a 9th competency cefr/skill/mediation used as a flat reporting rollup (B2B/teacher/admin only, never B2C; classification IRI already existed). Universal COMPUTE threshold >=2 samples (was 4 for drills; <2 = noise) across grammar/roles/drills/vocab/skills. THREE COMPUTATIONS kept separate: metric (>=2) != passed (band>=6 + >=80h effective-use gate for HR/level) != i+1 (a single weakness adjusts the loop). Attainment is DUAL-LEDGER: learner sees progress from day 1; HR/level gated at >=80 effective hours (anchored to CEFR/Cambridge guided hours). Measure!=Decide made CUMULATIVE: level = holistic global-achievement decided by the ENGINE (Global x5 + analytics x2, all on 0-10 with no 0-5 conversion, normalized total/pool*10; pool 130 today / 150 with pronunciation); one session never sets the level; the model observes and does not memorize. WRITING (option B): existing production rubric (grammar-accuracy+vocabulary-range+discourse-management+global-achievement) over en.wrt.* when built; NO cefr/skill/writing minted; not developed yet. AGENTS (D-1): three observing agents + a deterministic CODE consolidator (not a 4th LLM); corrector runs post-role-play and feeds the i+1 cards. Added a GDPR data-protection policy (pseudonymous UUID, no PII to the model, adapt-not-train, incident log). Purely policy/coverage; the 3 SRS IRIs (activity-type/card-pack, activity-type/chunk-in-context, ext/srs-schedule) remain pending mint. || v0.7.1 (approved by AE): +1 ADDITIVE rubric category — rubric/global-achievement, the holistic mark of the Cambridge English overall Speaking scales (the interlocutor's global-achievement scale, alongside the analytical criteria). Enables a Cambridge-aligned REPORTING VIEW over the 6-category diagnostic engine: bands 0-10 (finer granularity; 6 = meets the level, floor >=4, Cambridge 0-5 view = score/2), Grammar&Vocabulary reported combined at A2-B2 and separated at C1-C2, Pronunciation reported as one criterion (rolls up phonological-control + intelligibility; intelligibility kept as internal pass floor). Evidence honesty preserved: the engine measures FROM VOICE (ASR transcript + LLM-judge for grammar/lexis/discourse/interaction/global = Tier 1; pronunciation phonological detail is Tier 2/3, acoustic-tier-gated), so each criterion carries its evidence tier and nothing claims examiner-level precision the ASR does not have. Cambridge descriptors are cited and paraphrased for a business-adult context, NOT reproduced. Purely additive; nothing removed. || v0.7 (2026-08-10): +1 ADDITIVE rubric category — rubric/discourse-management (organisation, coherence, extended spoken turns) for full parity with the four official Cambridge English speaking criteria (Grammar&Vocabulary -> grammar-accuracy + vocabulary-range; Pronunciation -> pronunciation-phonological-control + intelligibility; Interactive Communication -> interaction; Discourse Management -> discourse-management). Band 1-3, MLLDE-decided, read against the level's Can-Do; acoustic evidence borrowed from ext/fluency-measures (speech-rate, pause-frequency, hesitation-rate) + transcript coherence. CEFR alignment: Coherence & cohesion / Overall spoken production. Scorecard is now 6 rubric categories. Purely additive; nothing removed. || v0.6 (2026-08-10): +8 ADDITIVE IRIs to carry the TK Coach teaching model (IPO) improvement on top of the v0.5 one-turn engine. VERBS: verb/answered (discrete scorable practice item). ACTIVITY-TYPES: activity-type/grammar-drill (S5 warm-up), activity-type/vocabulary-card (S4/SV spaced repetition). CONTEXT EXTENSIONS: ext/content-ref (target grammar/vocab point from the CEFR content inventory), ext/level-decision (demonstrated-level recalibration on verbs/progressed; self-declared level kept separately), ext/learning-target (i+1 target on verb/adapted). RESULT EXTENSIONS: ext/item-score (drill correctness, unaided → grammar-accuracy; mastery >=3/4 unaided), ext/srs-outcome (spaced-repetition result; vocab mastery when next interval >=7 days). Purely additive: no v0.5 IRI changed or removed. These connect the content layer (content/ inventory) and enable the model's two jobs — IMPROVE (rubric+then/now → i+1) and MAINTAIN (SRS retention). || v0.5 (2026-08-05): minted 10 first-class acoustic RESULT EXTENSIONS as measurement concepts — ext/phoneme-accuracy, ext/stress-accuracy, ext/rhythm-score, ext/intonation-score, ext/speech-rate, ext/pause-frequency, ext/hesitation-rate, ext/fluency-score, ext/intelligibility-score, ext/acoustic-confidence. Each defined in acousticMetrics with label/definition/dataType/range/unit/evidenceTier/CEFR-scale/usedBy/pedagogicalMeaning. calculationMethod owned by the acoustic engineer (MLLDE technology-agnostic). CEFR mapping: phoneme→Sound Articulation; stress/rhythm/intonation→Prosodic Features; speech-rate/pause/hesitation/fluency/intelligibility→Overall Phonological Control; acoustic-confidence=reliability. Granular extensions PREFERRED; v0.4 composites prosody-scores & fluency-measures retained as valid roll-ups. PROVENANCE: metrics are borrowed from speech-technology literature (Azure Pronunciation Assessment; Witt & Young 2000; Munro & Derwing 1995); MLLDE's contribution is the xAPI semantic model + CEFR alignment + pedagogical interpretation, not the metrics themselves. || v0.5 (2026-08-05): added the acousticMetrics catalogue — 10 first-class metric objects (phoneme-accuracy, prosody, rhythm, intonation, stress-accuracy, speech-rate, pause-frequency, hesitation-rate, fluency, intelligibility), each with definition, range/units, calculation method, evidence tier, xAPI carrier + JSON path, CEFR phonological-control scale, and pedagogicalMeaning (threshold → pedagogicalActions IRI). Metrics 1–9 measured by the engine; intelligibility decided by MLLDE. No new xAPI extensions minted — metrics reuse phoneme-scores/prosody-scores/fluency-measures/rubric-scores. New metric/* IRIs are catalogue identifiers, not statement carriers. || v0.4 (2026, approved by AE): two result extensions minted for the confirmed AE's Pronunciation Model v1 — prosody-scores (intonation·rhythm·stress → Prosodic features scale) and fluency-measures (speech rate·pauses·fillers·self-corrections); total 127 IRIs. v0.3 (2026-08-04, approved by AE): four incident types added from TK Coach hands-on evaluation — tutor-task-substitution, report-without-evidence, session-not-finalized, access-denied. v0.2: branding correction, APA references embedded. v0.1: initial 121-IRI registry. || v0.8.1 (2026-09-01, approved by AE): minted 3 IRIs for the audit demands (UX/UI demo audit) — ext/measure-model (context), ext/effective-time and ext/srs-schedule (result). NO new agents; NO scale change. Rule reaffirmed: descriptors feed lessons/practice, NEVER bands; only the evaluator emits bands. || v0.8.2 (2026-09-24, approved by AE): STANDARDS-CONFORMANCE FIX (no new concepts). H1 — the 7 reused ADL verbs (attempted, completed, passed, failed, progressed, interacted, asked) were written with https://adlnet.gov; corrected to the canonical http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/* (http:// and https:// are DISTINCT IRIs to an LRS, so the https form silently duplicated instead of reusing the ADL verb and broke metric universalisation — reuse-first rule enforced). H3 — declared the reserved void verb http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/voided in verbs.reused (already emitted in production, previously undocumented). answered (H2) left as an open authorial decision: keep minted or reuse ADL answered — unchanged in this version. Emitter must emit the same http:// forms. || H2 (2026-09-27, approved by AE): answered moved from minted to reused -> http://adlnet.gov/expapi/verbs/answered (ADL already defines it; keeps distinction from interacted).
_document.status: Design registry (production draft). Next step: convert to a formal xAPI Profile (JSON-LD, conformsTo https://w3id.org/xapi/profiles#1.0) and validate at https://profiles.adlnet.gov before publication.
_document.researchFinding: No official IRI vocabulary exists for CEFR skills, subskills or mediation (Council of Europe publishes descriptors as documents, not linked data). No language-learning xAPI profile exists in ADL's authored-profiles registry. Therefore MLLDE mints its own namespace, reusing established generic IRIs where semantics match, and records alignments to CEFR Companion Volume scales and ESCO/Europass as metadata.

_namespacePolicy.rationale: w3id.org is the free, community-run persistent-identifier service used by modern xAPI profiles (audio, cmi5, seriousgames all live under w3id.org/xapi/). Registering w3id.org/mllde is a single GitHub pull request, filed from the profeanaeslavaedtech GitHub account, and keeps IRIs stable even if a personal domain lapses.
rules: Reuse-first: if an established IRI (ADL, w3id profile) matches the meaning exactly, reuse it; never mint a duplicate.
One concept, one IRI: every skill, subskill scale, level, rubric category, extension, verb, incident type and pedagogical action has exactly one distinct IRI.
IRIs are identifiers, not links: they never need to resolve to a webpage, but each SHOULD eventually resolve to human-readable documentation.
Extension values are IRIs from this registry (e.g. cefr-level extension carries https://w3id.org/mllde/cefr/level/b1), so any LRS can interpret statements without MLLDE documentation at hand.

minted.definition: Made a pronunciation attempt at a declared target feature (phoneme, stress, intonation). Result carries phoneme-scores and/or model-imitation outcome.

minted.label: mediated
minted.definition: Performed a mediation activity: transformed or relayed content from a source for a recipient. Context carries the mediation scale IRI and the output-channel skill IRI.

minted.label: adapted
minted.definition: Actor is the teaching agent (human or AI): the learning path or assessment was adapted for the learner. Context carries the pedagogical-action IRI and the evidence that motivated it.

minted.label: Mission / authentic task
minted.note: The unit of authentic assessment (service encounter, negotiation…). Candidate to align with the ADL seriousgames profile — verify overlap on packaging.

minted.label: Pronunciation drill (Notice → Model → Invite → Move on)
Single spoken turn

minted.label: Grammar drill (controlled practice)
minted.note: A discrete controlled-practice item generated from a content-inventory grammar point (choose-form, transform, error-correct, meaning-match). Object of verb/answered; result ext/item-score feeds rubric/grammar-accuracy. Maps to demo screen S5 (warm-up). Added v0.6.

acousticMetrics._note: Acoustic Metrics — first-class xAPI RESULT EXTENSIONS (one IRI each), defined as measurement concepts. Each has label, definition, dataType, range, unit, evidenceTier, CEFR scale alignment, usedBy, and pedagogicalMeaning (threshold → pedagogicalActions IRI — MLLDE's decision layer, the differentiator). calculationMethod is OWNED BY THE ACOUSTIC ENGINEER; MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does not prescribe algorithms. RULE (Measure≠Decide): metrics are MEASURED by the engine and placed flat in result.extensions; the intelligibility BAND (pass floor) and every pedagogicalMeaning outcome are DECIDED by MLLDE. These granular extensions are PREFERRED for new statements; the v0.4 composites ext/prosody-scores and ext/fluency-measures remain valid roll-ups. See acoustic-profile-specification.md.

items.label: Phoneme Accuracy
items.definition: Degree to which produced phones match the expected IPA target sounds (accepted regional variants count as correct).
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: GOP over a forced alignment.
items.priorArt: GOP (Witt & Young, 2000); Azure AccuracyScore/PronScore; phoneme-level scores.

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Accepted variant (seseo/distinción, yeísmo, s-aspiration) → full credit, never lowered
Practice target — model the sound + invite retry (never a penalty)

items.label: Stress Accuracy
items.definition: Degree to which lexical and sentence stress fall on the expected syllables.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: detected vs expected stress placement.
items.priorArt: Prosody/stress in pronunciation assessment; Azure ProsodyScore (stress); ErrorType: unexpected break/monotone.

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Report-only at basic levels — feedback yes, gate no
Implicit recast — correct by modelling, flow preserved

items.label: Rhythm Score
items.definition: Degree to which syllable timing and speech rhythm reproduce target patterns.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: timing-regularity metrics (e.g. nPVI).
items.priorArt: Speech-rhythm metrics (e.g. nPVI; Grabe & Low, 2002); prosody research.

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Report-only at basic levels — feedback yes, gate no
Implicit recast — correct by modelling, flow preserved

items.label: Intonation Score
items.definition: Degree to which pitch movement (rising/falling contours) matches target intonation.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: pitch/F0 contour tracking.

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Report-only at basic levels — feedback yes, gate no
Implicit recast — correct by modelling, flow preserved

items.label: Speech Rate
items.definition: Speaking tempo of the learner's delivery.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: word count / net speaking time.
items.decidedBy: engine-measures → MLLDE decides (against a level-expected range)

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Report-only; set expected WPM range per level in D1

items.label: Pause Frequency
items.definition: How often the learner pauses (silent and filled pauses) per minute of speech.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: voice-activity detection over a duration threshold.

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Report-only — pauses are normal while planning
Graded hint / sentence starter to sustain the turn

items.label: Hesitation Rate
items.definition: Rate of disfluencies — hesitation markers (um, er, eh), repetitions and false starts.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: filled-pause / repair detection.
items.priorArt: Disfluency research (filled pauses, repairs, false starts).

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Offer a chunk/frame to reduce load

items.label: Fluency Score
items.definition: Overall fluency, combining continuity, pause behaviour, speech rate and repairs.
items.measures: Continuity; pause behaviour; speech rate; repairs (a composite).
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: composite of speech-rate, pause-frequency, hesitation-rate, self-corrections, onset latency.
items.priorArt: Azure FluencyScore; automatic fluency assessment literature.

items.label: Intelligibility Score
items.definition: Estimated probability that a native listener understands the utterance without effort. NOTE: this is the engine's ESTIMATE; the pass-floor intelligibility BAND (1–3) is decided by MLLDE (rubric/intelligibility), synthesising this with the NLU 'was the message understood?'.
items.usedBy: Voice Assessment Engine (estimate) → MLLDE (decides the band / pass floor)
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: comprehensibility model / listener-effort estimate.
items.decidedBy: engine-ESTIMATES the score; MLLDE DECIDES the intelligibility band (pass floor ≥ 4)

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Below floor — simplify + clarification-request loop; task does NOT pass yet

items.label: Acoustic Confidence
items.definition: Confidence that the acoustic engine has correctly measured the other metrics for this utterance. Distinct from ext/asr-confidence (transcription confidence).
items.measures: Reliability of the acoustic measurement itself.
items.calculationMethod: Defined by the acoustic engineer — MLLDE is technology-agnostic and does NOT prescribe the algorithm. Illustrative only: model posterior / SNR-based reliability.
items.decidedBy: engine-measures → MLLDE gates (low confidence → do not score, log incident)

pedagogicalMeaning.label: Low measurement confidence — do not score; ask to repeat; log incident/low-asr-confidence; exclude from aggregates (non-punitive)
Confident measurement — metrics may be scored

acousticMetrics._provenance: These acoustic metrics are ESTABLISHED in speech technology and pronunciation assessment (e.g. Microsoft Azure Pronunciation Assessment: AccuracyScore, FluencyScore, ProsodyScore, PronScore, phoneme/word scores, ErrorType; GOP after Witt & Young, 2000; intelligibility/comprehensibility after Munro & Derwing, 1995). MLLDE does NOT invent them. MLLDE's contribution is the SEMANTIC MODEL: formalising these borrowed measurements as interoperable xAPI result extensions, aligning each to a CEFR phonological-control descriptor scale, and attaching a pedagogicalMeaning (decision layer). Positioning: 'MLLDE adopts established acoustic pronunciation-assessment metrics reported in the speech-technology literature and formalises them as interoperable xAPI learning measurements aligned with CEFR phonological descriptors.' Borrowed = the metrics; NEW = the xAPI semantic model + the CEFR alignment + the pedagogical interpretation layer.
